evidence.moral: Biographical sources document El Saadawi's sustained feminist writing and advocacy against gender-based social and sexual oppression.
evidence.poder: Her record includes imprisonment, censorship, threats and exile connected to her public writing, making freedom of expression and political repression relevant.
evidence.religiao: Her writings criticized patriarchal uses and interpretations of religion. A numeric secular/religious placement requires direct review of her own texts rather than a biographical shortcut.
evidence.representacao: Her activism sought greater legal and social agency for women; the selected sources do not establish a complete institutional-democracy position.
evidence.estrutura: El Saadawi challenged authoritarian and patriarchal institutions but did not articulate a detailed federal-versus-centralized constitutional model; keep structural placement moderate.
evidence.imigracao: Her international feminist activism and critique of cultural essentialism support pluralism, though she did not center immigration policy.
evidence.diplomacia: Her public work relied on writing, international advocacy and cross-border feminist networks rather than militarism.
evidence.intervencao: She was critical of imperialism and authoritarianism, supporting skepticism toward coercive foreign intervention.
evidence.economia: Her socialist and feminist critiques linked women's oppression to class and economic inequality, supporting a substantial egalitarian public role.
evidence.controle: Her politics favored social provision and anti-capitalist reform more than laissez-faire, though not necessarily centralized command planning.
evidence.comercio: Her anti-imperialist critique supports skepticism toward unequal global economic relations rather than a simple free-trade position.
evidence.tecnologia: A physician and public intellectual, she accepted science and medicine while criticizing their patriarchal misuse; use a pragmatic moderate-to-positive technology stance.
